title: Make a new return reason impossible to miss

blocks.text: The shop gives customers a window, in days after delivery, to send an order back. The window depends on the reason they pick:

The `Reason` enum is generated from the returns service's schema, and that team adds a reason a few times a year. Last spring they added one, and for three weeks customers who chose it were quoted a window that nobody in this team had agreed to, until finance noticed.
Write `windowDays(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/RefundPolicy.java`, without touching the enum. When the next reason arrives, two things must hold:

items: once this project is built against the new enum, the build fails, with the compiler pointing at your method;
a copy of this class that was built before the reason existed, and meets it in production, throws rather than quoting any window.

blocks.text: About five lines in total. The tests compile your file themselves, once as it is and once with a reason added, and run the old build against the new enum.

cases.says: each of today's reasons gets the window the policy sets for it
once a reason is added to the enum, the class no longer compiles, and the error is that the switch doesn't cover every input
a build compiled before a reason was added still answers the old reasons and throws for the new one rather than returning a window

origin.section: A Constant Added After Compilation Reaches the Switch as MatchException

concepts: A switch expression over an enum that names every constant and has no default stops compiling when a constant is added; a default arm lets the new constant through.
A constant added to the enum after the switch was compiled reaches the default javac generated, which throws MatchException (IncompatibleClassChangeError when compiled for release 20 or earlier).
